h: Shabbos Minchah and the Quiet Joy of Complete Rest

p: and likewise the three prayers were instituted,
each prayer with its own wording,
according to the holiness of the meal,
This is not so on Yom Tov,
when all the meals are one holiness
and the wording of the prayers is one.
And the Minchah prayer of Shabbos
הוּא כְּנֶגֶד קְדוּשַּׁת יַעֲקֹב אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
corresponds to the holiness of Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom,
as corresponding to Yaakov Avinu, alav hashalom.
And in this prayer we say,
"Yaakov and his sons rest on it";
for at this prayer and at this meal
of Kudsha Brich Hu and Knesses Yisrael.
And for this reason the Shemoneh Esrei begins
"and find rest, each woman in the house of her husband."
And likewise the Beis HaMikdash is called "rest,"
יִחוּד קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
the union of Kudsha Brich Hu and Knesses Yisrael.
And in this prayer are mentioned
הוּא כּוֹלֵל קְדוּשַּׁת כָּל הַג׳ אָבוֹת
includes the holiness of all three Avos,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קעה, ב)
as it says in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 175b):
And why in the two prayers
is the holiness of the Avos not mentioned
neither at night the holiness of Yitzchak,
nor at Shacharis the holiness of Avraham?
that in the two prayers they instituted the wording
we do not say "They shall rejoice in Your kingship."
וְהוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (סִפְרֵי בְּהַעֲלוֹתְךָ)
And it follows what it says (Sifrei, Beha'alosecha):
"And on the day of your rejoicing" (Bamidbar 10:10)
there is no mitzvah of rejoicing
in accepting the yoke of the Kingdom of Heaven
the opposite of the yoke of a human kingdom,
which is a yoke without joy;
and this is the expression "your rejoicing."
And therefore in the prayers of Maariv and Shacharis
we do not mention the Avos,
since there is no mitzvah of rejoicing;
And likewise we say in the zemiros at night,
that it come through the light.
And likewise at the morning meal,
through which to come to joy.
This is not so at the third meal,
Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinah;
and it is "a rest of truth and faith,"
עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב (רַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא פִּנְחָס רל, א)
according to what it says (Ra'aya Mehemna, Pinchas 230a):
He is truth and She is faith.
For Yaakov Avinu is the middah of truth,
and his sons are in the aspect of faith,
"Just as there is in your heart only One,
so there is in our heart only One"
only in the aspect of faith.
And then, when there is the union and the rest,
then it is "the joy of his heart";
"And on the day of the joy of his heart"
this is the building of the Beis HaMikdash,
and it is called "the joy of his heart,"
for the joy is not revealed,
but the heart rejoices by itself.
And likewise we say in the zemiros of the third meal,
without any effort or any cause,
but rather "in which is the Will of Wills."
And then the two Avos too,
and therefore we say in it,
only with "Yaakov and his sons" is the main thing mentioned,
which is the rest and repose;
and the joy is only in the heart,
"the day of the joy of his heart."
